docs.text:
• phenix workflow: every flag of the command.
  • Configuration: the config kinds you put in phenix-configs/.
  • Experiments: managing the experiments a workflow creates.

docs.title: Builder
docs.text: Builder is the graphical topology editor in the phēnix web UI. You draw devices, switches and connections on a canvas, and when you publish, Builder writes the Topology config for you.

docs.title: What You Can Do
docs.text:
• Draw a diagram with devices, switches (one network each), connections, groups, notes and drawings, and arrange it by hand or with one of five automatic layouts.
  • Import a Topology or Experiment config as a new draft, or upload a diagram file, for example from another phēnix server.
  • Add devices from templates, kept in the diagram or in a shared library.
  • Check the diagram as you work, for issues such as an interface with no VLAN or two devices with one hostname.
  • Publish a Topology config, and optionally an Experiment config with one of its scenarios.
  • Go back: Builder saves each change, and Draft History restores an earlier snapshot.
  • Download a PNG or SVG picture, a draw.io file, a Gephi (GEXF) file, or a Topology YAML file.
  • Work from the keyboard with a command palette and shortcuts.

docs.title: How Builder Fits phēnix
docs.text:
A diagram lives in a draft on the phēnix server. Drafts aren't configs: the Configs page doesn't list them, and editing one writes nothing. Only Publish writes a Topology or Experiment config, so until then you can change as much as you want.

A published topology names its diagram. On the Configs page it has the tag builder, which opens the diagram in Builder again. An experiment runs from the Topology config, not from the diagram.

Positions, groups, notes, colors, icons and layers live only in the diagram. Publishing leaves them out, but a Builder JSON download keeps them.

docs.title: Where to Start
docs.text:
Click Builder in the navigation bar to open it.

  1. Do the Tutorial. It takes about 10 minutes and ends with a published topology and an experiment.
  2. Read the page for the feature you need. Each one links to a details page with the rules and limits.
  3. When something doesn't work, see Troubleshooting. Messages, codes, shortcuts and limits are in the Reference.

Note

Earlier phēnix releases had a different graphical editor, also named Builder. Builder converts its diagrams when you import or upload them (see Legacy Builder).

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Administration: Builder permissions, libraries and storage.
  • Configuration: the configs that Builder publishes.
  • Experiments: create and start an experiment from a published topology.

docs.title: Administration
docs.text: This page is for phēnix administrators. Every phēnix server has Builder, and roles control who can use it.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The builder use permission gives a user Builder: every draft and all three libraries. Drafts have no owner. A draft records who created and last changed it, but only for information.

To give a role Builder, add this policy to it (it takes no resource names):

- resources:
  - builder
  verbs:
  - use

builder use gives no access to configs. Of the built-in roles, only Global Admin and Builder have it. With authentication disabled, all users work as global-admin.

Builder hides or disables each control that a role doesn't allow, and the server checks each request anyway. Without builder use, there's no Builder link in the navigation bar, and /builder says "Your role does not include the Builder."

docs.title: The Builder Role
docs.text:
The built-in Builder role is for users who draw diagrams and publish them as topologies. Besides builder use, it has every configs verb on Topology/*, Scenario/* and Experiment/* only, and the schemas, topologies, scenarios, experiments and disks permissions that Builder uses (see Builder (builder)).

Each time phenix ui starts, it makes sure that the role exists and has builder use. It doesn't touch other roles, so add the builder policy to each other role that needs Builder, then assign roles on the Users page (see Updating Users).

docs.title: What Each Task Needs
docs.text:
builder use alone covers all work on drafts, the libraries, the Inspector fields, and Upload of a Builder document. Other tasks also need configs permissions:

Task Also needs Import a stored config configs get on the config, and topologies or experiments list on its name Import a config file configs get and create Publish configs update to use Publish, and create (new) or update (existing) on each config that it writes Preflight the permissions of each check

The full table lists every task.

docs.title: Example Role
docs.text:
The example role Topology Designer can work on drafts and the libraries, but can't publish, import a config file, delete a topology, store a scenario file, or create the configs of a package. Someone with the Builder role then publishes its drafts. To add the role:

  1. Download topology-designer.role.yaml.
  2. Store it with phenix config create.
  3. Assign it on the Users page.

Warning

Don't use "*/*" in the configs policy of a role. It also matches User and Role configs, so a user could read password hashes.

phēnix copies a role's policies into a user when you assign the role, so after you change a Role config, assign the role to its users again.

docs.title: The Libraries
docs.text: The server keeps one template library, one layer set library and one icon library, which all Builder users share and change. No role can change the built-in templates, the server collections, the built-in layer set Purdue Model, or the icons that phēnix added from template files. Duplicate makes a copy of a read-only template or layer set that users can change. phēnix logs each library change with the user name.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Drafts, published documents and the libraries are records in the phēnix store, not configs, so phenix config list and the Configs page don't list them. Their limits are in Limits.

At start and every hour, phēnix deletes the published and stored documents that nothing references anymore. Clean up… in the Builder settings does the same right away, and also deletes each draft with no change since its last publish. It shows what it would delete and asks first (see Cleaning up storage).

docs.title: Template Files on the Server
docs.text:
To give all users the same node templates, put template files in the template directory of the server. When phenix ui starts, it reads each file as one read-only collection. A file has the format that the Node Templates tab downloads (see the example node-templates.yaml).

The directory is <base-dir.phenix>/builder/templates, by default /phenix/builder/templates. To change it, set base-dir.builder-templates with the flag --base-dir.builder-templates, the environment variable PHENIX_BASE_DIR_BUILDER_TEMPLATES, or the config file (see Settings):

base-dir:
  builder-templates: /etc/phenix/builder-templates

phēnix reads the .yaml, .yml and .json files in the directory, and skips (and logs) a file that isn't valid. It only reads them at start, so restart phenix ui after you change them. Custom icons in a file become server icons, which no user can rename or delete (see Template files on the server).

docs.title: The builder-doc Annotation
docs.text: A Topology config names its diagram in the builder-doc annotation, a map with up to three keys: digest and id, which Publish writes, and path, which you write yourself for a Builder file. A topology shows the published document that the annotation names, or else the file at path. phēnix refuses a Topology config whose annotation isn't valid (see The builder-doc annotation).

docs.title: A Builder File Beside a Topology
docs.text:
A topology in a repository can keep its diagram there too, as a Builder JSON or YAML file. Name the file in the annotation:

apiVersion: phenix.sandia.gov/v1
kind: Topology
metadata:
  name: pump-station
  annotations:
    builder-doc:
      path: /phenix/topologies/pump-station/pump-station.builder.json
spec:
  ...

To make such a config:

  1. Open the draft in Builder, or upload the Builder file.
  2. Click Download > Topology YAML.
  3. Set metadata.name.
  4. Add the annotation. Don't change the spec.
  5. Store the config with phenix config create.

The Published Diagrams tab then lists the topology with the File tag. phēnix reads the file each time someone opens the diagram, so a git pull that changes the file changes the diagram. The file must be below the base directory (/phenix, or the base-dir.phenix setting) and outside the VM mount directory (see Which files phenix reads).

Warning

The name of a topology doesn't protect its Builder file. A user who has configs get, and create or update, on any one topology name can store a topology there with any path below the base directory, and then open that file. Only keep a Builder file below the base directory if each such user may read it (see Who can read a Builder file).

Publish never writes the file. It stores a published document and writes digest and id beside the path, so the file is out of date until you replace it with Download > Builder JSON.

docs.title: API
docs.text: Scripts use the same REST API as the web UI, under /api/v1, and the interactive API docs at /docs/ describe each route under the Builder tag. Each route needs builder use, and a route that reads or writes configs also needs the configs permissions of the matching web UI task (see REST API).

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Administration: Details: every permission, store record, file rule and REST route.
  • User Authn/Authz in phēnix: roles, users and tokens.
  • API: how to send a token with a request.
  • Troubleshooting: what users see when a permission is missing.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text: This page shows how to draw a diagram, using the Riverside Water draft of the example lab. Keep one idea in mind: a switch is one network, and a connection puts an interface on that network.

docs.title: What a Diagram Is
docs.text:
A diagram describes one Topology config, but publishing writes only some of it:

In the diagram In the Topology config A device A node in spec.nodes, with its settings A switch A network, whose name is the VLAN of its interfaces A connection An interface with the network's name as its vlan A device from an included topology Nothing. includeTopologies names that topology Notes, groups, drawings, colors, icons, layers and templates Nothing

docs.title: Add Devices
docs.text: Nodes & Objects, in the left column, lists what you can add. Click an item or drag it to the canvas, or press Ctrl+K (⌘+K on macOS) and pick Add device. Device has default settings, and the five built-in templates under Templates fill in more (see Built-in templates). An external device is hardware, such as a PLC: phēnix starts no VM for it, and its interfaces say which VLANs the hardware is on (see External Nodes).

docs.title: Networks
docs.text:
A switch is one network. To add one, click Switch under Nodes & Objects, set its Name in the Inspector, and click Apply. Renaming a network changes the VLAN of each interface on it.

A network can also have a VLAN alias (1 to 4094, written to vlans.aliases when you publish with an experiment), a Subnet and a Gateway. A new network gets a suggested subnet, which you can change or clear. With a subnet, each static interface you connect gets the next free address, and Assign addresses fills in the ones that have none (see Subnets and addresses).

docs.title: Connect an Interface
docs.text:
To connect ws-03 to CORP, use any of these:

  • Drag from the + handle under ws-03 (which adds a new interface), or from an unconnected connection point on its side, to the CORP switch.
  • Select ws-03, click Add connection in the Inspector header, pick the switch CORP (CORP), and click Connect.
  • In the Inspector, click Add interface under Network, enter Address 10.10.20.103 and VLAN CORP, and click Apply.

CORP has no subnet, so type the address of eth0 yourself or give CORP a subnet first. A typed VLAN never gives an address, and one that names no network leaves the interface unconnected.

To disconnect an interface, click Disconnect next to it under Connection points, or select the connection and press Delete (⌫ on macOS). The interface stays with no VLAN, which blocks publishing until you connect or remove it. To hide connections on your canvas only, see Hiding connections.

docs.title: Edit Device Settings
docs.text:
Change a device's fields in the Inspector or the Node Editor, then click Apply (see The Editor). Changing an interface's Interface kind clears the interface, so set the kind first. Routes and Firewall rulesets are under Network, and the vrouter app applies them on a Router or Firewall when the experiment starts. Labels and annotations are under More settings.

To duplicate a device, select it and press Ctrl+D (⌘+D on macOS). The copy, such as historian-01-2, keeps every setting but not its connections, so you'll get a warning until you give it its own hostname and address and connect it.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: A note is text on the canvas, and publishing ignores it. Click Note under Nodes & Objects, enter the Text in the Inspector, and click Apply.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
A group is a box with a title around nodes; it moves with its nodes, and publishing ignores it. To group nodes, select them (Shift-click to add to the selection), then click Group in the toolbar or press Ctrl+G (⌘+G on macOS). Ungroup (Ctrl+Shift+G, or ⇧+⌘+G on macOS) deletes the group and keeps its nodes. Dragging a node onto a group doesn't put it in; use Move to group in the Inspector header instead.

Auto-group in the toolbar makes groups for you: By network, By name (hostnames that share a stem, such as web-01 and web-02), or By name pattern… (see Grouping by a name pattern).

docs.title: Drawings
docs.text: Rectangles, circles, icons and lines are drawings. Publishing ignores them, and they take no connections. Add one under Nodes & Objects, then set its Label and other fields in the Inspector (see Shapes, icons and lines).

docs.title: Colors, Line Styles and Icon Size
docs.text:
Most things on the canvas have color fields in the Inspector, and a switch's Edge Color colors its whole network (see Colors). Line style, on a network or a single connection, is Auto, Solid, Dashed, Dotted or Dash-dot. Auto picks a pattern from the network's place in the diagram, so networks differ even without color.

Icon size in the Diagram section of the Inspector draws icons Small, Medium or Large, and a device, switch or group can have its own size (see Icon size).

docs.title: Icons
docs.text: Pick the icon of a device, group or icon drawing under Icon in the Inspector. It's just a picture and changes no setting (see Built-in icons). To use your own image, pick Custom icon… at the end of the list (see Custom icons).

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: A layer has an ID from 0 to 99 and a label, and can have an icon, a color and node matchers. Layers are only for the picture, and an import sets none. To put a device or switch at a layer, select it and pick one under Layer in the Inspector. A node matcher does this for you by the device's fields, for example hostnames that start with plc- (see Node matchers). Edit layers… under Layer opens the layers editor.

docs.title: Layer Sets
docs.text: A layer set is a reusable list of layers in the server's library. In the layers editor, Use a layer set gives the diagram a linked copy of a set, and Save to layer set saves your changes back as its next version (see Layer sets).

docs.title: Example: The Purdue Model
docs.text: The built-in set Purdue Model has a layer for each Purdue level, from "L5 Enterprise" (ID 6) down to "L0 Process" (ID 0) (see Purdue Model layer set). To use it, open the layers editor, pick Purdue Model (built-in) under Use a layer set, and click Apply. To see it in a full diagram, upload lakeside-treatment.builder.json and pick By layer in the layout menu.

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
The layout menu in the toolbar arranges the whole diagram:

Layout What it does Network cards A card for each network, the switch above its devices. ELK layered Clusters each network's switch with its devices, left to right. By layer Puts the layers from top to bottom, highest ID first (see By layer). Dagre Devices beside their switch, networks along the connections. Standard Every device in a row above the switches.

ELK layered suits most diagrams. Layouts keep groups together, and right after a layout runs, the menu offers Restore previous layout.

docs.title: Arrange by Hand
docs.text: Drag a node or several selected nodes, press Shift with an arrow key to move them 10 pixels, or enter X and Y under Position in the Inspector and click Move. Turn on Snap to grid (off by default) to put the nodes you drag or add on the grid (see The grid).

docs.title: Copy, Paste, Duplicate and Delete
docs.text: Copy, Paste and Delete are in the toolbar, and Duplicate is in the command palette. Copy and Paste work between drafts opened in the same browser tab. A connection is pasted only along with both of its nodes, so copy a device together with its switch. Deleting a device also deletes its connections.

docs.title: Undo and Redo
docs.text: Undo and Redo in the toolbar only reach the changes since you opened the draft in this tab. To go back further, use Draft History (see Undo and redo).

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
A diagram lists up to 20 Scenario configs, and an experiment published with the topology uses one of them (see Publishing). To add the stored scenario riverside-water:

  1. Click Scenarios in the toolbar.
  2. Under Scenarios of this diagram, check riverside-water.
  3. Click Save scenarios.

Checking a scenario doesn't change it on the server. The same dialog can also edit, create and upload scenarios (see Scenarios).

docs.title: Included Topologies
docs.text:
riverside-water includes the topology corp-services, so dns-01 and ntp-01 show up with a dashed border and the text "Included from corp-services". You can move them, but you can't edit, delete or connect them, or rename their network. To change dns-01, change corp-services and import riverside-water again.

To edit them in the diagram itself, select one and click Combine into a new draft in the Inspector. That opens a new draft with them as normal devices, which publishes as a new topology (see Making included devices editable).

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Building a Diagram: Details: addressing, drawings, colors and layouts in depth.
  • Layers: Details: node matchers, layer sets and the layers editor.
  • Limits: the limits of layers, patterns, icons and scenarios.
  • Topology: the Topology config that publishing writes.

docs.title: Drafts
docs.text: A draft is a diagram saved on the phēnix server, along with its history. Builder saves each change you make, and only Publish writes a config.

docs.title: The Drafts Page
docs.text:
Click Builder in the navigation bar to open the drafts page.

Commands opens the command palette (Ctrl+K, or ⌘+K on macOS). The Node Templates and Icons tabs are covered in Templates and Icons.

The Drafts tab lists every user's drafts, most recently changed first, and any Builder user can open, change and delete any of them. Publish on a card opens the Publish diagram dialog without the editor (see Publishing from the drafts page). To find a draft, type part of its name or a user name in Filter drafts.

docs.title: Create a Draft
docs.text:
• Blank diagram opens a new draft named "Untitled topology". It adds a number to the name when a draft has it.
  • Import makes a draft from a Topology or Experiment config, stored in phēnix or in a file.
  • Upload makes a draft from a Builder JSON or YAML file, pasted text, a published diagram, or a legacy Builder diagram.

See Import, Upload and Download for the details. To edit a published diagram, see The Published Diagrams Tab.

docs.title: Open a Draft
docs.text:
Click Open on the draft card, or use the command palette:

  1. Press Ctrl+K.
  2. Enter open draft and press Enter.
  3. Enter part of the name and press Enter.

To go back to the list, click Drafts in the editor header. While a draft is open, the address bar shows a link to it that works for any Builder user.

docs.title: How Drafts Save
docs.text:
There's no Save button: Builder saves each change to the server as you make it, and the save state in the toolbar shows where your changes are, for example All changes saved (see Save states). Save now (Ctrl+S, or ⌘+S on macOS) sends them right away.

If the server can't be reached, Builder keeps your changes in this browser and you can keep editing. It sends them on its own once the server answers again, or when you click Retry saving (see Working offline).

docs.title: Draft History
docs.text:
Each saved change is a snapshot. Draft History in the toolbar lists the snapshots, newest first, with Current marking the one you're on.

To go back, click Restore on an earlier snapshot. The newer snapshots stay, and a notice above the toolbar says how many your next change will delete. Return to latest goes back to the newest one, and Save newer history as a new draft copies it to a new draft.

Warning

A change after a restore or an undo deletes all newer snapshots, including other users' snapshots.

Undo and Redo also move the current snapshot, one change at a time. To delete a snapshot (but not the current one), click Delete in its row, then Delete snapshot; this can't be undone. A snapshot marked Automatic holds Inspector changes you didn't apply, which Builder saved when you left, published or downloaded the draft.

docs.title: Duplicate a Draft
docs.text: Duplicate on a card makes a new draft from the current diagram and opens it. The copy has "(copy)" after its name, no history, and no link to a topology or experiment, so publishing it asks for a new topology name and makes a new topology.

docs.title: Delete a Draft
docs.text:
1. Click Delete on the draft card.
  2. Click Delete draft.

This deletes the draft and its history for good, but not the configs it published.

docs.title: Select Several Drafts
docs.text: Check the cards, then click Download selected to save a Builder JSON file for each, or Delete selected to delete them all after one question. You can also select cards with the keyboard.

docs.title: The Published Diagrams Tab
docs.text:
This tab lists each topology that has a Builder diagram, and Open shows the diagram read only.

To change it, click Edit as a draft (the builder tag on the Configs page does the same). Builder opens the draft that already published the diagram or was made from it, or else makes a new one. That draft can publish to the topology again. If the diagram was published with an experiment, Exp on the card and in the editor toolbar opens the experiment.

Delete on a card deletes the Topology config from phēnix, but not the drafts and experiments made from it. A card tagged File gets its diagram from a Builder file on the server and has no Delete.

docs.title: The Layers Tab
docs.text: This tab is the server's library of layer sets (named lists of layers and their options), shared by all users. The built-in Purdue Model set has the seven Purdue levels, from L0 Process to L5 Enterprise; to change it, Duplicate it and change the copy. Set default makes a set the server's default, and each Blank diagram starts with a copy of it (see The Layers tab).

docs.title: Damaged Drafts
docs.text: A draft that this server can't read has Delete but no Open (see Damaged drafts).

docs.title: Logging Out
docs.text: Logging out deletes unsent changes from the browser, so wait until the save state says All changes saved first (see Logging out).

docs.title: The Same Draft in Two Tabs
docs.text: Don't open one draft in more than one browser tab: if both tabs hold unsaved changes, Builder can save only one tab's changes (see Same draft in multiple tabs).

docs.title: Draft Merging
docs.text: If another user saves the draft before your changes reach the server, Builder merges their changes with yours, field by field. When changes clash, it shows This draft changed on the server and you pick which changes to keep (see Draft merging).

docs.title: The Draft Limit
docs.text: At its draft limit, the server refuses new drafts. To make space, delete drafts or click Clean up… in Settings (see Limits).

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• The Editor: the toolbar, Inspector and settings of an open draft.
  • Publishing: turn a draft into Topology and Experiment configs.
  • Troubleshooting: save, merge and offline problems.

docs.title: The Editor
docs.text: The editor is where you draw and change a diagram. Builder saves each change and checks the diagram as you work. The editor has five areas: the header, the toolbar, Nodes & Objects on the left, the canvas, and the Inspector on the right.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
The header has Drafts (back to the drafts page), the diagram name, the vCPU and memory totals of the devices that phēnix starts, and a count of each kind of item. Click a count to select everything of that kind. Then come the checks button and the view buttons.

To rename the diagram:

  1. Click Edit diagram name (the pencil). A field replaces the name.
  2. Type the new name.
  3. Press Enter.

The diagram name isn't the topology name. You pick that when you publish.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
Most toolbar buttons do what their names say. Ungroup removes a selected group but keeps its nodes, and Auto-group groups nodes by network or by name. Upload opens a diagram file as a new draft. Exp opens the experiment you published, while it exists, and Draft History restores an earlier snapshot of the draft.

The save state comes last, for example All changes saved. If a save fails, Retry saving shows up next to it (see Drafts).

docs.title: Canvas
docs.text:
• Click a node or a connection to select it. Shift+click adds a node to the selection or removes it. Click an empty spot to clear the selection.
  • Drag a node to move it, or drag an empty spot to pan.
  • Zoom with the mouse wheel or the zoom buttons at the bottom left.
  • To connect a device to a switch, drag from the device's connection point to the switch (see Diagrams).

Hover over a device or a switch to see its info tooltip. Reset view in the header resets the zoom, the minimap and the side columns, and doesn't change the diagram (see Canvas).

docs.title: Side Columns
docs.text: Click an item in Nodes & Objects (Device, Switch, Note, Group or a drawing) to add it, or drag it onto the canvas. Templates lists the device templates (see Templates and Icons). You can widen, hide or resize this column and the Inspector (see Side Columns).

docs.title: Inspector
docs.text: The Inspector shows the fields of the selected node or connection. With nothing or several items selected, it shows the diagram's own fields, such as Name, Description, Layers, Notes and Scenarios (see With Nothing Selected).

docs.title: Editing a Node
docs.text:
Select a node to see its fields. A field marked * is required, and a field that isn't at its default has a Default button.

To change fields:

  1. Change one or more fields. A bar at the bottom says Unapplied changes, with Apply and Cancel.
  2. Click Apply, or press Enter in a field. Builder changes the diagram and saves it.

If you select another node without applying, the Inspector applies the valid changes and drops the rest. Icon, the colors and Layer take effect right away, without Apply (see Fields That Take Effect at Once). Custom icon…, at the end of the Icon list, opens the Custom icons dialog (see Templates and Icons).

You can move a device from an included topology, but you can't change it, and nothing in a published diagram can change (see Fields You Cannot Change). Other kinds of nodes have their own fields. A switch's Assign addresses fills in the addresses of its network (see Addresses of a Network).

docs.title: Node Editor
docs.text:
The Node Editor shows the fields of one node in a large dialog, along with the node's checks. To open it, double-click the node, or click Open Node Editor in the Inspector header.

Search fields finds a field by its label, such as memory, or by its YAML path in the Topology config, such as network.interfaces[0].vlan (see Searching the Fields). Empty the box to see all the fields again.

Apply applies all your changes as one Undo step and closes the Node Editor. If you cancel with unapplied changes, Builder asks before it throws them away.

docs.title: Checks and Warnings
docs.text:
Builder checks the diagram as you edit it. Each node and connection with an issue gets a mark on the canvas: a cross for an error, or a triangle for warnings only.

To fix an issue:

  1. Click the checks button. The Diagram checks dialog lists the errors, then the warnings.
  2. Click Go to beside the issue. The canvas selects its node, and the Inspector shows it.
  3. Fix the field.

You can't publish until you fix the errors. Some warnings also block Publish, and the dialog says so (see What Blocks Publishing). Some issues have a Fix button, and Undo reverts each fix (see Fixing an Issue in One Step).

Builder also warns about settings that phēnix accepts but doesn't apply the way the diagram shows them (see Rulesets and Addresses and Device Settings).

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
Preflight, at the bottom of Diagram checks, asks the phēnix server to check the saved draft against the server and its cluster. Its four checks (Host capacity, Networks, Disk images and Scenario apps) write nothing and start no VMs or experiments.

To run Preflight:

  1. Click the checks button in the header.
  2. Under Preflight, tick the checks.
  3. Optional: in Experiment (optional), enter the name of the experiment.
  4. Click Run. Builder saves your latest changes first.

Each check shows Passed, Failed or Unavailable. Unavailable means Builder couldn't do all of the check, for example because it couldn't connect to minimega (see Preflight).

docs.title: Command Palette
docs.text:
The command palette runs commands and finds things. To open it, click Commands in the header, or press Ctrl+K (⌘+K on macOS).

  • Type words to find commands, for example layout.
  • Type @ to find a node by its hostname, address, VLAN, label or description (see Finding Nodes).
  • Type # to find a network by its name or VLAN alias.
  • Type t:, c: or i: for node templates, template collections or custom icons, and ? to see all the prefixes.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: To see all the shortcuts, click Shortcuts in the header, or press ? outside a text field. The ones you'll use most are Ctrl+Z (Undo), Ctrl+D (Duplicate), Delete and N (add a device). On macOS, use ⌘ in place of Ctrl. The full list is in the Reference, and Change shortcuts in the sheet gives any command other keys (see Customizing Shortcuts).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: To open Builder settings, click Settings in the header, or press Alt+Shift+S (⌥+⇧+S on macOS). Changes apply right away. The settings belong to your browser, not to the diagram, and stay after you log out. For each setting and its default, see Settings.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
• ?, N and the zoom keys work without Ctrl until you turn off Single-key shortcuts (see Single-Key Shortcuts).
  • Clean up…, in Builder settings, deletes the published, unchanged drafts of all users and the stored data that nothing uses (see Administration).
  • Edit layers…, in the Inspector, the Node Editor, Builder settings and the command palette, opens the layers editor for the open diagram.
  • Focus mode hides the phēnix navigation bar, so Builder fills the window. Click Focus mode in the header, or press Ctrl+Shift+F (⇧+⌘+F on macOS).
  • The theme button cycles through System, Light and Dark. It changes only Builder (see Themes).
  • You can use Builder with only a keyboard, or with a screen reader (see Accessibility).

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• The Editor: Details: rules and limits of each part.
  • Checks and Preflight: Details: each warning, fix and preflight check.
  • Command Palette and Shortcuts: Details: search prefixes and custom shortcuts.
  • Diagrams: add, connect, group and lay out nodes.

docs.title: Import, Upload and Download
docs.text:
Builder uses three words for three tasks:

  • Import makes a draft from a Topology or Experiment config, stored in phēnix or in a file.
  • Upload opens a file that is already a diagram as a new draft: a Builder document, a Builder package, a published diagram or a legacy Builder diagram.
  • Download saves the open diagram as a file, in one of seven formats or as a Builder package.

Apart from Create on this server in a Builder package upload, none of these change a config: that's what Publish does (see Publishing). For the rules and the less common cases, see Import, Upload and Download: Details.

docs.title: Import a Stored Topology
docs.text:
1. On the drafts page, click Import.
  2. Keep Source set to Stored config and Source kind set to Topology.
  3. In Source name, select riverside-water. The dialog shows Included topologies, because riverside-water includes corp-services.
  4. Click Import. The dialog shows 1 warning: the 2 devices from corp-services are read only.
  5. Click Continue to editor.

The draft gets the name of the config. An import without warnings opens the editor straight away.

docs.title: Import an Experiment
docs.text: Set Source kind to Experiment, and select the experiment (such as riverside) in Source name. The draft lists the experiment's stored scenario (when your role can list it), never the copy in the experiment, and the experiment's VLAN aliases become the VLAN alias of each network. It doesn't keep the VLAN range or experiment fields such as baseDir, and warns about them. Files that experiment apps injected into VMs at start are left out without a warning, but the topology's own injections stay. The import also removes the values that phēnix added when it created the experiment (see Importing an Experiment).

docs.title: Import a Config File
docs.text:
1. Click Import.
  2. Set Source to Config file.
  3. In Topology or Experiment config, choose the file, for example pump-station.topology.yaml. It can be JSON or YAML, up to 5 MiB.
  4. Click Import.

A draft from a config file can only publish a new topology, even when a stored config has the same name.

Note

Builder keeps each ${NAME} and ${NAME:default} in the file as written. Unlike phenix config create, it never fills them in from the server's environment, so edit such values in the draft before you publish.

docs.title: Import Options
docs.text:
When the topology includes other topologies, the dialog offers:

  • Keep included nodes read only (the default). Publishing keeps the includes.
  • Combine into one new topology, which copies the included nodes into the diagram as ordinary devices. Publishing creates a new topology.

For a stored topology that you don't combine, Create a new topology as a copy is also offered. A copy or a combined import proposes a New topology name ending in -copy or -combined, and the draft can't update the source topology.

docs.title: From the Configs Page
docs.text: On the Configs page, the tag builder marks a topology with a Builder diagram and opens it in Builder, and builder legacy marks one from the legacy Builder. A topology without a diagram has Import into Builder in its viewer, which opens the Import dialog set to that topology.

docs.title: What an Import Keeps
docs.text:
An import keeps every node, as a device with all of its settings, in the order of the config. Each VLAN becomes a network with a switch, and each interface connects to the switch of its VLAN. Devices of included topologies are read only, unless you combine them. The config's annotations show in the Inspector with nothing selected, but publishing doesn't write them.

Devices are laid out in rows on a grid with the switches below them (the Default layout). A config has no subnets or gateways, so networks get none. A warning names every other change (see What an Import Keeps).

docs.title: Upload a Builder Document
docs.text:
A Builder document is the file that Download > Builder JSON or Builder YAML saves. To open one as a new draft:

  1. On the drafts page or in the editor toolbar, click Upload.
  2. Keep Source set to File.
  3. In Builder document file, choose the file, for example pump-station.builder.json.
  4. Click Upload. The new draft has the name in the document.

Source can also be Paste text, Published diagram, or Legacy Builder diagram or Topology, which converts a diagram of the legacy Builder (see Legacy Builder). Upload refuses configs, template and layer set files, files that aren't JSON or YAML, and files over 5 MiB, and the dialog tells you why.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
1. Open the draft.
  2. Click Download.
  3. Click a format. The browser saves the file.
  4. Click Close.

Download Formats says what each file holds, what opens it, and how it's named. Builder itself can't open a draw.io or Gephi (GEXF) file.

Topology YAML saves even when the diagram can't be published yet, and lists each reason, so it's a quick way to see what blocks publishing. phenix config create stores the file as a topology without its diagram. To store both, publish the draft.

docs.title: Move a Diagram With a Builder Package
docs.text:
A Builder package moves a diagram to another phēnix server. It's one JSON or YAML file with the diagram, the configs and icons that you tick, and a list of everything the diagram needs, such as scenarios, included topologies and disk images. It never holds disk images, apps or files, only their names.

To download a package:

  1. Click Download.
  2. Under Builder package, tick Scenario configs, Included topologies, Custom icons or Disk-image requirements.
  3. In Package format, select JSON or YAML.
  4. Click Builder package.

To upload it on the other server:

  1. Click Upload.
  2. In Builder document file, choose the package file.
  3. Click Upload. The dialog lists each item that the diagram needs as Present, Missing, Different or Not checked.
  4. For each missing config that you want, tick Create on this server. Builder never replaces a config that the server has.
  5. Click Continue to editor. Builder creates the ticked configs, adds the missing icons, and opens the diagram as a new draft.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• File Formats: each Builder file, its size limit and its JSON Schema.
  • A Builder File Beside a Topology: keeping a diagram in a repository next to its topology.
  • Troubleshooting: imports and uploads that don't work as expected.
  • Configuration: phenix config create and the configs that an import reads.

docs.title: Legacy Builder
docs.text: Earlier phēnix releases had a different graphical editor, also named Builder, built on mxGraph. It opened at /builder in a new browser tab. This release doesn't include it, but you can convert its diagrams.

docs.title: What Changed
docs.text:
Legacy Builder Builder Where phēnix keeps a diagram XML in the builder-xml annotation of the topology A draft on the phēnix server. Publish stores the diagram and names it in the builder-doc annotation What writes the topology Save to phēnix Publish (see Publishing) Tag on the Configs page builder legacy builder REST routes POST /builder/save, /api/v1/builder/topologies, /api/v1/experiments/builder Removed (see REST API)

Legacy topologies still run, since phēnix never read the diagram to run an experiment. Convert one only if you want to edit it as a diagram.

Warning

On the Configs page, the annotation shows as builder-xml: <SNIPPED>. phēnix keeps the diagram as long as that line is unchanged. If you delete the line, phēnix deletes the diagram.

docs.title: Converting a Stored Topology
docs.text:
Import converts the diagram of a stored topology that has builder-xml and no builder-doc:

  1. In the phēnix navigation bar, click Builder.
  2. Click Import.
  3. Keep Stored config and the Source kind Topology.
  4. In Source name, choose the topology. Its name ends in "(legacy Builder diagram)".
  5. Click Import.
  6. If the dialog lists warnings, click Continue to editor.

On the Configs page, the builder legacy tag and the viewer's Import into Builder button open the same dialog.

The draft takes its nodes from the topology. The old diagram supplies only each node's position and icon (matched by hostname), the switches, the VLAN IDs, the notes and the groups. Edit the draft as needed, then replace the legacy diagram:

  1. Click Publish.
  2. In Topology name, enter the name of the topology.
  3. Click Update topology.
  4. Click Update topology again.

Nothing changes on the server until you publish. Publishing deletes builder-xml, writes builder-doc, and changes the tag to builder. It deletes the old diagram even if the import couldn't read it.

Only the draft imported from the topology itself can replace its legacy diagram. Any other draft has to publish under a new name. If the topology or its legacy diagram changes after the import, publishing is refused (see When the source config changed).

docs.title: Converting a File
docs.text:
Upload converts a legacy diagram in a file:

  1. On the drafts page or in the editor toolbar, click Upload.
  2. Under Source, choose Legacy Builder diagram or Topology.
  3. In Legacy diagram or Topology file, choose the file.
  4. Click Convert.
  5. If the dialog lists warnings, click Continue to editor.

The file can be up to 5 MiB, and must be one of these:

  • An XML file from Save to Disk in the legacy Builder. Its root element is mxGraphModel (or a bare root).
  • A Topology config, as YAML or JSON, with the builder-xml annotation, such as one downloaded from the Configs page.

draw.io files (mxfile) and compressed or base64-encoded diagrams don't convert. For a Topology config without the annotation, use Import instead.

A diagram file without its topology has only the node settings that the diagram itself holds. A draft converted from a file always publishes a new topology, even if a stored one has the same name.

docs.title: What Is Converted
docs.text:
Devices, switches, connections, text (as notes) and rectangles or containers around nodes (as groups) carry over, at twice their old spacing. A line between two devices was a direct connection; Builder adds a switch for its network. A VLAN ID becomes the network's VLAN alias when it's a number from 1 to 4094.

For a diagram without a topology, a placeholder such as $DEFAULT_VCPU takes the diagram's variable, else the legacy default (DEFAULT_MEMORY 2048, DEFAULT_VCPU 1, DEFAULT_VM_IMAGE ubuntu.qc2, DEFAULT_ROUTER_IMAGE vyos.qc2).

Styling (colors, fonts, shapes, arrows), edge labels, waypoints, layers (merged into one), page settings, tooltips, links, images, shapes without text, and lines that don't join a device to a network are left out.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
The dialog lists warnings before it makes the draft. Most of them only say what changed or what Builder placed for you. These are worth a look:

Warning What it means "The Builder could not read the legacy diagram of topology NAME (…). …" The draft has the topology's nodes on a grid, and publishing deletes the old diagram "1 node of the legacy diagram is not in the topology. The Builder did not import it: …" The topology changed after the diagram was last saved. The draft follows the topology "Used the legacy defaults for variables the diagram does not define: …" Check the values in the Inspector "1 placeholder has no value in the diagram. The Builder kept it as text: $NAME." Replace the text in the Inspector before you publish "1 item has settings that the Builder could not read. The Builder did not import it: …" A node in the diagram has damaged settings, so the draft doesn't have it "1 node has interfaces that the Builder could not read. The Builder did not import these interfaces: …" The node stays, without those interfaces "The Builder did not import 1 link whose node has no interface on that network: NODE to NETWORK." None of the device's interfaces uses that network "VLAN ID VALUE of network NAME is not a number from 1 to 4094. …", "Network NAME has more than one VLAN ID …" or "VLAN ID ID occurs on networks A and B. The Builder kept it only for A." A network has no VLAN alias, or kept only one of the IDs it had "The Builder renamed node "OLD" to "NEW": a hostname cannot hold spaces." Spaces became hyphens. Networks get the same treatment

docs.title: Keeping a Copy of the Old Diagram
docs.text: Before you publish, download the topology from the Configs page. The file holds the XML, and Upload can convert it again. To open the old editor, use phēnix 1.0.0 or an earlier release.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Import, Upload and Download: the other ways to bring a topology into Builder.
  • Troubleshooting: import and upload problems.
  • Configuration Files: Topology configs and their annotations.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: Publishing turns a draft into a Topology config, and optionally an Experiment config with one of the scenarios that the diagram lists. Builder publishes the last saved snapshot, and the server checks it again before it writes anything.

docs.title: Before You Publish
docs.text: Fix the errors, and the warnings that block publishing. Publish applies and saves any valid changes still open in the Inspector, and names the ones it can't apply. You'll find Publish in the toolbar, in the command palette as Publish…, and on each card of the drafts page (for the permissions, see What each task needs).

docs.title: Publish a Topology
docs.text:
To update the topology riverside-water from the Riverside Water draft:

  1. Open the draft.
  2. Click Publish.
  3. Under What to publish, keep Topology only.
  4. Below Topology name, click Use riverside-water. The hint says "A topology with this name exists. Publishing updates it."
  5. Read Checks. It says what is ready to publish.
  6. Click Update topology. Builder asks "Replace topology riverside-water?".
  7. Click Update topology again.
  8. Click Close.

A config name can only hold letters, numbers, _, @, . and -.

docs.title: What the Topology Holds
docs.text: The Topology config holds the settings of each device, and the network of each connected interface as its vlan. Everything else, such as positions, groups, notes, drawings, icons, layers, and the Subnet and Gateway of a network, stays in Builder.

docs.title: What Publishing Changes
docs.text: What publishing changes, above the buttons, previews the effect on the server.

docs.title: Create or Update
docs.text:
The hint under Topology name says whether publishing creates or updates that topology, and the button names the action (see Publish hints and buttons). A draft can update an existing topology when it published that topology, is an import of it, was opened from its published diagram, or is an upload of a Builder document from such a draft. A copy, a combined import, or an import of a config file can't, so the dialog refuses the name.

Warning

You can't undo an update: phēnix keeps no earlier version of a config. To go back, restore an earlier snapshot in Draft History and publish again.

An update keeps the topology's other annotations and adds builder-doc.

docs.title: The Result
docs.text: The dialog lists each stage and its result (see Publish results). If a stage fails, fix the cause (stop a running experiment, for example), click Back and publish again with the same names. Stages that are already done show skipped, so nothing is written twice.

docs.title: Publish a Topology and an Experiment
docs.text:
To update riverside-water and create the experiment riverside-lab:

  1. Open the draft.
  2. Click Publish.
  3. Under What to publish, select Topology and an experiment.
  4. Below Topology name, click Use riverside-water.
  5. In Experiment name, enter riverside-lab.
  6. Keep Experiment scenario at riverside-water.
  7. Click Update topology and create experiment. Builder asks "Replace topology riverside-water?".
  8. Click Update topology and create experiment again.
  9. Click Close.

Publish writes the VLAN alias of each network to vlans.aliases of the experiment. A new experiment's name can't be all, and on some servers it can have at most 15 characters (see Experiment names).

A draft can only update the experiment it comes from, or the one it published. Stop the experiment first, because an update runs the configure stage of the apps. An update also removes the host pins of devices that are no longer in the topology (see Host pins).

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: Publish adds the topology to the topology annotation of each listed scenario, and refuses if a listed scenario doesn't exist or you can't read it (see Scenarios).

docs.title: What Blocks Publishing
docs.text:
Errors block publishing, for example two devices with one hostname. So do these warnings, which the Publish dialog lists as errors:

  • an interface with no network and no VLAN, on a device that isn't external
  • two interfaces on one network with the same IP or MAC address
  • a hostname that phēnix refuses: one character, all, all digits, or phenix on a Windows device
  • an ospf interface on a vyatta, vyos or linux Router or Firewall with no network.ospf, or an ntp-server label that names no interface with an IP address
  • a device that isn't external, with no drive

Under Checks, click Go to beside an issue to fix it. Here, a copy of historian-01 has an interface with no VLAN (see Example: Riverside Water expansion).

Tip

Download > Topology YAML saves the topology that Publish would write, and lists every issue that blocks publishing.

docs.title: Publish Again
docs.text: After each set of edits, publish again with the same names. Builder won't publish again if another draft published the topology since, or someone changed it outside Builder (with phenix config edit, for example). The hint under Topology name says which. Either way, edit a draft of the topology as it is now (see Edit a Published Topology), or publish under another name.

docs.title: When the Source Config Changed
docs.text:
If the config a draft comes from changed after Builder made the draft, Publish refuses the draft under any name, and the dialog shows a warning at the top. To keep your work:

  1. Make a draft of the config as it is now. Click the edit button of the topology on the Configs page, or import it again.
  2. Copy the changed devices from the old draft, and paste them into the new draft.
  3. Connect the pasted devices again. A pasted device keeps its settings but not its connections.

docs.title: Included Topologies
docs.text: The published topology names an included topology, such as corp-services, without copying its devices. A diagram imported with Combine into one new topology publishes them as its own. If the diagram and an included topology use the same hostname, Publish refuses (see Included topologies).

docs.title: Edit a Published Topology
docs.text: On the Configs page, click the builder tag in the topology's row, or click Edit as a draft on the Published Diagrams tab. Builder opens the draft that published it, or else a draft of the published diagram.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
• A topology can name a Builder file as its diagram (see Publishing to a topology that names a Builder file).
  • A draft imported from a legacy Builder topology replaces the legacy diagram when it publishes back (see Converting a stored topology).
  • The Scenarios dialog writes Scenario configs to the server at once, and Cancel doesn't undo them.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Publishing: Details: the rules and messages behind each step.
  • Experiments: start the experiment you published.
  • Configuration Files: the Topology config that Publish writes.
  • Troubleshooting: what to do when a publish fails.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: These are the tables that the other Builder pages link to, from save states to error codes. The details page of each feature explains the rules behind them.

docs.text:
The save state sits next to Draft History in the editor toolbar (see How drafts save).

The server can't be reached or didn't answer in time. This browser keeps your changes. Keep working. See Working offline. Offline: 2 changes not stored anywhere yet. Keep this tab open. Could not save: someone deleted this draft from the server. Select Download to keep a copy of the diagram. Another user deleted the draft. Click Download (see Downloading), then upload the file as a new draft. You cannot save changes to this draft Your role no longer includes Builder. Ask an administrator for Builder access (see Permissions). Click Download to keep a copy. Could not save your last change. … When you fix the diagram, the Builder saves it again. The server refused the diagram, for example for two devices with one hostname. The message names the error. Fix it (see Checks and warnings). The next change saves the diagram. Your next edit saves the diagram as shown. Could not save. … Remove part of the diagram, or select Download to keep a copy. The diagram is too large for the server to save. The message says why. Remove part of the diagram, or click Download to keep a copy. Could not save your changes. … Saving retries automatically. The server refused the save for another reason, which the message names. Wait, or click Retry saving.

Retry saving shows up when you're offline, or when another try can fix a failed save. It sends the waiting changes right away.

"Canvas" means the canvas, its nodes and its connections (not the zoom buttons). A few things the table doesn't show:

  • From the canvas itself, the arrow keys go to the node nearest the middle of the view. While connections are hidden, they go only to nodes.
  • Delete deletes the focused item, or the whole selection when the focused item is part of it.

docs.title: Publish Hints and Buttons
docs.text:
In the Publish diagram dialog, the hint under Topology name says what publishing will do with that name, and the button names the action. The hint under Experiment name works the same way (see Create or update).

Hint Button "Publishing creates a new topology." Create topology "A topology with this name exists. Publishing updates it." Update topology "A topology with this name already exists. This diagram cannot update it. …" None: Builder won't publish. Enter another name. "A topology with this name changed after this diagram published it. Publishing would overwrite that change. …" None: Builder won't publish. See Publishing again. "… This diagram replaces its legacy Builder diagram." or "… Builder could not read its legacy Builder diagram. Publishing removes it." Update topology. See Replacing a legacy Builder diagram.

docs.title: Publish Results
docs.text:
After a publish, the dialog lists each stage and its result (see The result).

Stage What it is Results document The published copy of the diagram, on the Published Diagrams tab created, or skipped when you publish again and the publication was already complete topology The Topology config created, updated, or skipped when the config already holds this snapshot scenario The topology annotation of each listed scenario updated, with the changed scenarios, or skipped experiment The Experiment config, with Topology and an experiment created, updated or skipped draft The draft records what it published ok, or skipped when you publish again and the publication was already complete

The headline is one of these:

Headline What it means "Published. Every stage succeeded." Every stage succeeded. "Published with failures. …" A stage failed after the server wrote earlier ones. Fix the cause, click Back, and publish again with the same names. The stages that already succeeded show skipped. "Publish failed. It wrote no configs." A stage failed before the server wrote any config, and the list shows which. Fix the cause, click Back, and publish again.

When the server refuses the publish before it writes anything, the form stays open, and Checks gives the reason after "Could not publish the diagram."

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text:
Each issue that Builder reports has a code, a stable name for the rule it breaks, such as node.hostname.duplicate. The editor checks and the Builder REST API use the same code for the same rule, so a script can act on the code and ignore the message.

A code is lowercase words joined by dots, and a word can contain hyphens (not-found). The first word names what the rule is about, such as node, edge (a connection) or layerset (a layer set). A released code keeps its meaning, and a new rule gets a new code.

docs.title: Issues
docs.text:
Each warning and error is an issue with these fields:

Field Value code The code of the rule severity error if the issue refuses the request, warning if not message The text that a person sees path The location in the document, such as nodes[3].device.hostname, when the issue is about a part of it nodeId, edgeId, networkId The ID of the node, connection or network, when the issue is about one field The device field, such as spec.network.interfaces.0.vlan, when the issue is about one

Codes gives the default severity of each code. Some issues block only publishing, such as an interface without a VLAN. A draft may keep them, so the editor shows them as warnings on the canvas, and the Publish diagram dialog shows them as errors.

An unknown key in an object of the document (document.field.unknown) is an issue at its path. A value of the wrong type is an issue only where the editor also checks the type, such as a number in createdBy (metadata.user.not-text). The server refuses other values of the wrong type, such as a node position that is text, with a message of its own.

docs.title: Errors of the REST API
docs.text:
When a Builder route refuses a request, the JSON body gives the code in code, with message and cause. For a document that fails the checks (document.invalid), or a draft that only publishing refuses (publish.blocked), issues lists each warning and error:

{
  "code": "publish.blocked",
  "message": "topology lab cannot be published: interface \"eth1\" of device \"web\" has no VLAN: connect it to a network, or type a VLAN for it",
  "cause": "validating topology projection: interface \"eth1\" of device \"web\" has no VLAN: connect it to a network, or type a VLAN for it",
  "issues": [
    {
      "code": "interface.vlan.missing",
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "interface \"eth1\" of device \"web\" has no VLAN: connect it to a network, or type a VLAN for it",
      "path": "nodes[2].device.spec.network.interfaces[1]",
      "nodeId": "4113dfc0-f4be-57f9-8115-6cecd1f1aea3",
      "field": "spec.network.interfaces.1.vlan"
    }
  ]
}

A refusal about a scenario that the draft lists (publish.scenario.*) names that scenario in metadata.scenario.

These are the HTTP statuses of the codes. A refusal without a code of its own gets the request.* or server.* code of its status.

Status Codes 400 request.invalid, publish.target.invalid 403 request.forbidden, layerset.read-only 404 request.not-found 405 request.method-not-allowed 409 request.conflict, draft.conflict, draft.snapshot.current, template.item.read-only, publish.topology.exists, publish.topology.missing, publish.topology.not-source, publish.topology.changed, publish.topology.file-mismatch, publish.topology.file-changed, publish.experiment.exists, publish.experiment.missing, publish.experiment.not-source, publish.experiment.changed, publish.experiment.running, publish.source.changed, publish.include.clash 412 request.stale, draft.stale, template.item.stale, layerset.stale 413 request.too-large, draft.limit, layerset.library.full, package.too-large 422 request.unprocessable, document.invalid, publish.blocked, publish.topology.invalid, publish.experiment.invalid, publish.experiment.reserved, publish.experiment.name-too-long, publish.experiment.unmergeable, publish.include.hostname, publish.scenario.missing, publish.scenario.not-listed, publish.scenario.invalid, import.name.invalid, import.name.source, layerset.default.unknown, layerset.invalid, package.invalid 500 server.error 503 server.busy

OPTIONS on a Builder route gets 204 and the same Allow header as a 405 answer for that path, and does nothing else.

Where else issues show up in answers:

  • In package.invalid, each issue has a package.* code, or, for the package's document, a document code at a path below document.
  • A publication that goes through lists its warnings in warnings. A partial publication lists its failures in errors.
  • The Topology YAML download (POST /builder/export/topology) lists issues in warnings and publishBlockers. publishBlockers has one issue for each check that only publishing makes, with the code of its first issue.
  • POST /builder/package lists its package.* warnings in warnings.

The dependencies of POST /builder/package/resolve are data, not issues, and have no codes. The warnings of an import or a legacy diagram conversion (POST /builder/generate, POST /builder/legacy, and the source.warnings of a document) are plain text, without codes.

document has no ID. metadata.id.invalid error The document ID is not a UUID. metadata.name.too-long error The document name is longer than 512 bytes. metadata.name.control error The document name createdBy or updatedBy holds a control character. metadata.time.not-text error createdAt or updatedAt is not text. metadata.time.invalid error createdAt or updatedAt is not a UTC time of the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. metadata.notes.not-list error The diagram's notes are not a list of text. metadata.notes.too-many error The diagram has more than 100 notes. metadata.note.not-text error A note   • REST API: the Builder routes.

docs.title: Templates and Icons
docs.text: A device template holds everything a new device starts with: its icon, colors, layer and the whole node spec. A custom icon is an image of your own on a device, a group or an icon drawing. For the rules and the less common operations, see Node Templates: Details and Custom Icons.

docs.title: Where Templates Live
docs.text: Place What it is This diagram Templates saved in the diagram, which go everywhere the diagram goes. Library One library on the phēnix server, shared by all its users. Built-in Five read-only templates (see Built-in Templates). Server Read-only collections from template files that an administrator put on the server.

docs.title: Add a Device From a Template
docs.text:
Under Templates in Nodes & Objects, click a template or drag it onto the canvas.

The new device gets the template's hostname (numbered when the name is taken, such as plc-2), icon, icon size and layer, and a connection point for each interface, but no connections. Later changes to the template don't change the device. A library or server template also adds a linked copy of itself to This diagram.

docs.title: Make a Diagram Template
docs.text:
To save ws-01 of Riverside Water as a template of the diagram:

  1. Select ws-01 on the canvas.
  2. Click New device template, the + beside Templates.
  3. Change Template Name from ws-01 to Engineering workstation.
  4. Enter CORP workstation with CAD tools in Template Description.
  5. Click Save to diagram.

The template keeps everything of the device except its connections, and Undo reverses the save. With no device, or several nodes, selected, it starts from a plain device.

In the template's menu, Save to library adds a copy to the library and links the template to it. Delete doesn't ask first, but Undo brings the template back.

docs.title: Linked Templates
docs.text:
A linked template is a diagram template copied from a library or server template. A mark under it, such as Update available or Deleted from library, tells you when it needs your attention.

To update a linked template:

  1. Click Update on its mark, in its menu, or in the Inspector.
  2. Read the question. It says if the update replaces your changes to the template.
  3. Click Update template.

Devices made from the template don't change. When two or more linked templates have a newer version, Update all in the Inspector updates them all. Unlink ends the link and keeps the template as it is.

docs.title: The Template Library
docs.text:
Click the Node Templates tab on the drafts page, or Node Templates library beside Templates in the editor.

Show picks the list: all library templates, the ones with missing disk images, a collection, the built-in templates, or a server collection. A read-only card has View and Duplicate instead of Edit and Delete.

Save in the template editor sends the template to the server, so Undo can't reverse it. Delete asks first and deletes the template for all users. Diagrams keep their copies, which then show Deleted from library.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text:
A collection is a named group of library templates, and a template can be in several. To make one:

  1. Click New collection.
  2. Enter a Name.
  3. Click Create collection.

To fill it, select templates under All library templates, then pick the collection in Add to collection. While a collection shows, Edit collection changes its name and description, and Delete collection deletes it but keeps its templates.

docs.title: Template Files
docs.text:
A template file holds one collection of templates, as YAML or JSON, with a copy of each custom icon that its templates name and the server has. Download on a card, Download selected and Download collection each save one. To import one:

  1. Click Import templates on the Node Templates tab.
  2. Select the file. Builder describes it, for example "Plant floor: 2 templates and 1 custom icon."
  3. Click Import.

The templates go into a new collection named after the name in the file. For the format, see File Formats and the example node-templates.yaml.

docs.title: Server Collections
docs.text: Each template file in the server's template directory becomes a read-only collection, shown as Server: and its name (see Template Files on the Server). Duplicate collection copies it into the library, where you can change it.

docs.title: Custom Icons
docs.text:
All users of the server share one icon library. To use a custom icon:

  1. Select the device, the group or the icon drawing.
  2. In the Inspector, click Icon.
  3. Select Custom icon… at the end of the list.
  4. In the Custom icons dialog, click Use on a listed icon, or click Upload icon… and select an image file.
  5. For an upload, enter the icon name, then click Add icon.

A custom icon keeps its own colors in both themes, so use an image that is clear on light and dark backgrounds. For the files that Upload icon… takes, see Uploading an Icon.

The Icons tab of the drafts page lists the built-in and server icons. You can view and download them there, and delete the ones that users uploaded. Rename in the Custom icons dialog renames an uploaded icon, and the old name keeps working. Deleting an icon changes no diagram: its nodes show their built-in icon until someone uploads an icon of that name.

A Builder JSON or YAML download carries a copy of each icon that the diagram names, so it shows them on another server (see The Diagram and Its Icons).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: What you might see when something goes wrong in Builder, and what to do about it. The save states, codes and limits are in the Reference.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
For what each permission allows, see Permissions.

What you see Why What to do No Builder link in the navigation bar, or "Your role does not include the Builder." Your role has no builder use permission. Ask an administrator for the Builder role or the builder policy. A button such as Publish or Import is missing or grayed out, or "Your role cannot publish diagrams." in the command palette Your role doesn't allow that task (publishing needs configs update), or it's a published diagram, which opens read only. See What each task needs and Published diagrams. "Only Builder can edit this configuration" on the Configs page The topology has a Builder diagram, and your role has no builder use. Ask for the builder policy. "Topology … does not exist, or you do not have permission to read it." The topology was deleted, or your role can't list it. Ask for configs list and topologies list on it. "You cannot save changes to this draft" Your role no longer includes Builder. Ask for the permission, and click Download to keep a copy.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: What you see Why What to do "Offline: …" The server can't be reached or didn't answer in time. The browser keeps your changes. Keep the tab open, or click Retry saving. See Working offline. "This draft changed on the server" Someone saved a newer version first, and the changes can't merge on their own. Click Review and merge, Save my history as a new draft or Discard mine and load the server version. See Draft merging. "This draft is also open in another tab" The draft is open in two tabs. Close one. If both have unsaved changes, pick one in Choose which changes to save. "Could not save: someone deleted this draft from the server. …" Another user deleted the draft. Download a copy, then upload it as a new draft. "Could not save your last change. …" The server refused the diagram (two devices with one hostname, say). The message names the issue. Fix it; the next change saves. The sign-in page opens while you work Your session ended (by default after 24 hours). Log in. Changes the server didn't have yet are lost. See Logging out. A new draft is refused, with a hint to delete drafts or run Clean up… The server holds 2,000 drafts, its limit. Delete drafts, or run Clean up… in Settings.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: What you see Why What to do "N errors block publishing" under Checks The diagram has errors, or a warning that blocks publishing (such as an interface with no VLAN). Click Go to next to each issue and fix it. See What blocks publishing. "A topology with this name already exists. This diagram cannot update it. …" The draft didn't come from that topology and never published to it. Use another name, or import the topology and edit that draft. See Publish again. "A topology with this name changed after this diagram published it. …" The topology was changed outside Builder after this draft published it. Import it again, or use another name. "This diagram comes from topology …. … Publish refuses this diagram under any name. …" The source config changed after Builder made the draft from it. Make a new draft from the config and copy your changes over. See When the source config changed. "Could not publish the diagram. Scenario … does not exist.", "… does not have permission", or "Not found on the server" in the Scenarios dialog A listed scenario doesn't exist, or your role can't read or update it. Create the scenario, ask for access to it, or clear its checkbox and click Save scenarios. See Scenarios. "Phenix cannot publish topology …: node … is in this topology and in its included topology …" The diagram and an included topology share a hostname. Rename one of the devices. "Published with failures. …" A stage failed after earlier ones were written, for example because the experiment is running. Fix the cause, click Back, and publish again with the same names. See Publish results.

docs.title: Import and Upload
docs.text: What you see Why What to do Upload refuses a Topology or Experiment config, a template file or a layer set file Each has its own place. Use Import with Config file, Import templates on the Node Templates tab, or Upload layer set… on the Layers tab. "Could not convert the legacy diagram. …" The file isn't a legacy diagram, or it's a Topology config without builder-xml. See Converting a File. A package upload shows Missing, Different or Not checked items The server lacks the item, has another version, or can't check it. Tick Create on this server for a missing config in the package. Builder adds missing custom icons itself; add other items yourself. See Uploading a package. phenix config create, phenix config apply or phenix config diff refuses a file as "not a configuration" It's a Builder document, package, template file or layer set file. Add it in Builder instead. See Builder documents.

docs.title: Other Problems
docs.text: What you see Why What to do "A newer version of phenix may have saved it." on a draft card, the template library or a layer set A newer phēnix saved it, so this one can't read it. Use that version. A draft can also be deleted: see Damaged drafts. "Auto layout failed. The layout engine could not start.", "… could not load the layout engine. …", or "The Builder could not check the pattern." in Auto-group A proxy or content security policy may be blocking the layout engine. Reload the page. Ask the administrator to let the proxy serve the phēnix scripts and allow same-origin workers (Availability). A Preflight check shows Unavailable Your role lacks its permission, Builder can't reach minimega, the server lists no disk images, or the check took over 20 seconds. Read the cause under the check; the others still run. See Preflight. Icon shows "(custom icon not found: the node shows its built-in icon)" The icon was deleted, or the diagram came from another server. Upload an icon with that name. See Custom icons. "The layer set has a newer version. Update from the layer set first." Someone saved the layer set after the diagram copied it. Click Update from layer set (this replaces your changes to the copy), redo your changes, then Save to layer set. "A library holds at most 200 templates." when you save a template The library is full. Delete templates nobody uses. See Limits.
